text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a few cross-node residency blips during the prefill load test. some prefixes lost a lease briefly and later got double-evicted. not full outage but caused tail latency spikes.

jon: ugh. any obvious repro steps? logs/trace ids?

maria: attaching a small trace snippet i pulled from the canary: request id 0x7f9a. sequence: prefetch -> transfer -> demote -> eviction; handoff returned success but the recipient never updated epoch before demote.

ravi: that sounds like a classic transfer race where transfer_residency RPC returns before local epoch persist. can we make transfer atomic w/ epoch CAS?

anne: quick thought — do we need to change the contract so transfer is 2-phase: prepare (reserve token) + commit (persist epoch and ack)? current single RPC leaves a window.

maria: agreed. i sketched a minimal API change below that avoids a heavyweight global lock. open to bikeshedding names.

maria: ```proto
service PrefetchService {
  rpc PrepareResidencyTransfer(PrepareRequest) returns (PrepareResponse);
  rpc CommitResidencyTransfer(CommitRequest) returns (CommitResponse);
}

message PrepareRequest { string tenant; string prefix; int64 from_epoch; int64 to_epoch; string transfer_token; }
message PrepareResponse { bool ok; string transfer_token; }
message CommitRequest { string transfer_token; }
message CommitResponse { bool ok; }
```

jon: lifecycle: recipient must persist to local store before Commit ack. if recipient crashes after Prepare but before Commit, origin keeps lease until timeout. that avoids double-evict.

ravi: how long is the timeout? we need to pick a sensible default and metric it. also consider backlog: many pending prepares could bloat metadata.

maria: proposal: default prepare lease = 30s, configurable per-pool. metric: residency.prepare_pending_count, residency.prepare_latency_ms, residency.commit_failures_total.

anne: will this interact with shard rebalancer? rebalancer might move prefix while prepare pending. we should add a check: prepare rejects if rebalancer epoch != expected, return RETRY_WITH_EPOCH.

jon: ops play: we must add observability and a canary rollout. plan: 1) enable prepare/commit feature flag on canary nodes; 2) run prefill load for 2h; 3) monitor prepares pending, commit latency, eviction spikes.

maria: test plan notes: unit test for crash-after-prepare (simulate recipient crash and verify origin keeps residency), integration test that injects rebalancer-epoch-mismatch and ensures prepare rejects.

ravi: any perf cost? two RPCs per handoff could add p99. suggest coalescing prepare+commit in fast path when both nodes are in same AZ and SSD ack is fast; still keep 2-phase for cross-host.

anne: we can add an optimization: TransferHint header. if hint == "local-fast-path" the RPC may do atomic persist + return commit in same call (single RPC). fallback to prepare/commit for cross-node.

maria: here's a sample onelinercurl to simulate prepare->commit for manual test: 

maria: ```bash
curl -X POST http://canary-prefetch/prepare -d '{"tenant":"t1","prefix":"p-123","from_epoch":42,"to_epoch":43,"transfer_token":"tok-1"}'
# expect {"ok":true,"transfer_token":"tok-1"}
curl -X POST http://canary-prefetch/commit -d '{"transfer_token":"tok-1"}'
```

jon: sounds good. can we gate by flag and add a runtime metric that counts double-evict prevented? e.g., residency.double_evict_prevented_total.

maria: yes — add that plus a counter for prepare timeouts (residency.prepare_timeouts_total).

evict-bot: ALERT: eviction-spike detected on canary pool cp-7 at 2029-07-21T09:48Z — eviction_rate +420% over baseline.

anne: that's the same window. okay we should block global rollout until we confirm crash-after-prepare handled.

ravi: can someone sketch migration steps for in-flight leases? we need to be careful when rolling origin nodes to avoid leaving dangling prepares.

maria: migration sketch: 1) enable idempotent prepare tokens cluster-wide (server accepts duplicate prepares) 2) roll origin nodes with short grace window 3) monitor prepare_pending_count drop to zero before enabling commit optimization.

jon: also add sanity-check query: GET /residency_status?prefix=p-123 returns {owner, epoch, pending_transfer:?}. useful for human ops during canary.

maria: good call. i'll add that to the PR and include a small dashboard: prepare_pending, commit_latency_p50/p99, double_evict_prevented, prepare_timeouts.

anne: ok — next action owners? maria drafts RFC update + migration checklist. ravi will add tests. jon will own canary rollout and dashboard. i'll triage alerts during canary.

maria: thanks — i'll open PR w/ protos and tests by EOD. ping if you want to pair on tests. :thumbsup:

jon: thanks!
